sources_considered.why: Explains specific benefits of training-data access and distinguishes them from other forms of auditor access.
Independent output-based evaluation identifies linguistic discrimination, limiting an absolute reading of the claim.
Demonstrates a method for tracing selected training data through black-box outputs.
The licensing audit concerns accessible datasets and does not isolate the effects of nondisclosure on societal outcomes.
Relevant bias research, but the selected ChatGPT study more directly documents output-based evaluation.

receipt.public_excerpt: Access to data helps auditors trace problems and assess fair use.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper identifies concrete audit benefits from access to training data, supporting the proposed mechanism. It does not establish that nondisclosure prevents all the claimed assessments or quantify a substantial effect on every outside mitigation effort.

Researchers identified discrimination by prompting the models and evaluating their responses. This challenges the reading that no bias can be identified without dataset disclosure, but does not measure propagation through society under widespread deployment.

The study demonstrates tracing selected, marked data through generated outputs without internal model access. This limits an absolute impossibility claim, but does not establish the full extent of creators’ uncompensated use or harm.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved comparison isolates training-data disclosure and measures its effect on reliable assessment of societal bias propagation.
The evidence does not establish the extent of individual creators’ exploitation.
The magnitude and breadth of impairment to outside mitigation remain unmeasured.
